kurz: After cooking, wait a few minutes before cutting. Much less juice runs onto the board.
bild_im_kopf: Like fizzy water after shaking: opened straight away it gushes out; wait a moment and it stays in the bottle.
was_passiert: Right after cooking the juice is thin and the fibres are under tension. As it cools, the juice gets a little thicker and less runs out when cutting. At the same time the temperature inside rises a little more ([[nachgaren|carry-over cooking]]).
warum_wichtig: In one test, a pork roast rested for 10 minutes lost around 60 % less juice than one cut straight away.
schritte: Move the meat from the pan to a board or rack.
Cover loosely, not tightly, otherwise the crust turns soft.
Rest steaks for about 5 minutes, roasts for 10–20 minutes.

mythos.behauptung: Without resting, all the juice runs out.
mythos.richtig: Some always runs out. Resting reduces it a lot; after about 10 minutes, waiting longer brings little more.
